-B E F O R E -
Hon'Ble The Chief Justice Mr. Vijay Bishnoi Hon'Ble Mr. Justice Kaushik
Goswami 09.12.2024 (Vijay Bishnoi, Cj)

This writ appeal is filed by the appellant being aggrieved with the order dated 26.04.2024 passed by the learned Single Judge in WP(C) No.2193/2023,
whereby the learned Single Judge has closed the writ petition without adjudication, while observing that the grievance raised by the appellant of insufficient land acquisition compensation can only be addressed by availing the statutory remedy as prescribed under Section 3G(5) of the National Highways Act, 1956.

Mr. S.K. Talukdar, learned counsel for the appellant has submitted that, as a matter of fact, the appellant has not raised the grievance about the insufficient land acquisition compensation but has approached the Writ Court only with the contention that the compensation determined by the authorities concerned has not been paid to him in full and only a part payment is released.
Page No.# 3/3 It is noticed that in response to the writ appeal, an affidavit is filed on behalf of the Deputy Commissioner, Biswanath (presently District Commissioner, Biswanath), wherein in Paragraph 10 it is specifically mentioned that the compensation required to be paid to the appellant in view of acquisition of his land is determined as ` 79,59,204/-.

However, out of the said amount, `
46,00,074/- has already been paid to the appellant and the balance amount of ` 33,59,131/- is required to be paid to him.

In view of the specific admission made on behalf of the District Commissioner, Biswanath, we direct Mr. N. Das, learned Junior Government Advocate, Assam appearing for the District Commissioner,
Biswanath to instruct the District Commissioner, Biswanath to release the due amount to the appellant, as admitted by him in the counter affidavit filed on 08.11.2024, within a period of 4(four)
weeks from today.
